account: The RL-Zero-Math weight change is small (0.24 % of weight norm) and works through the top 8 paired input-output singular directions of each matrix (12 % of the change, 0.07 % of weight norm), directions that the base's own activations on step-by-step text already drive 8-11x more than random ones and that LM-judge and code rewards also produce; added to the base at 1.5x they reproduce RL (456 vs 457 of 500 on MATH-500, 200.25 vs 200.0 of 328 on hard328, 48.25 vs 50.5 of 136 on fresh2026).

These directions change each sample in two ways: they switch its opening from answer-first to deliberative ('Okay, let's see'), and in a graded way they make the derivation RL-like (longer and checked, stopping instead of looping or running to the cap, with fewer slips), so the 1.5x edit is right more often than a fresh base sample even where the base already finishes (36 % vs 23 % on base-finished-wrong hard328 problems) and captures 0.88 of RL's per-sample gain on problems the base never solves in 4 samples.

The untrained base already holds the opening (a 3-token cue, a self-drawn 'Okay' opening or a one-tensor hand edit takes it from 224 to 397-411 of 500, level with RL step 100 at 418 with the same cap rate and right answers only 1.15x the cued base's length against 1.61x for final RL), which is why inference alone gives 77-78 % of RL's gain on MATH-500 and on non-math questions and 53-58 % on code, and why the cue adds only 1.7 points to step 100.

Sampling and votes add reliability only where the base already samples a right answer, because its wrong answers mostly scatter (26 % pair agreement), so 81 % of RL's MATH-500 gap is on problems the base solves at least once in 4 and a vote over 6 base samples matches one RL sample, while at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 the cued base loops and the token budget eats those points.

What inference cannot reach is the derivation change on problems outside the base's sample reach (on hard328 the base has no right sample on 26 of the 36 problems RL's vote wins, so RL stays 8.8 points ahead under the vote), the part RL steps 100 to 2,800 add (+42.5 of 500), which needs RL's own input-output pairs (shifted pairs, random, Think-SFT directions, self-distillation, examples and Wait-steering give nothing) and whose slip part is domain-specific (Code-RL directions add +7.0 points of pass rate among finished code answers, Math-RL directions +1.5).

Imitation of long traces (Think-SFT) is a different change that runs longer and abstains at the cap instead of guessing (precision among finished answers 0.87 against RL's 0.69 on hard328), so it beats RL only on long answers, and RL's change adds on top of it (Think-SFT + 2x RL delta 231.5 vs 209 of 328) by turning Think-SFT's cap hits into finished answers, about half of them right.

consequences.claim: Sentences 1-2 say the 1.5x top-8 edit makes each derivation RL-like (longer and checked), not only right more often. So on hard328 problems that both solve, the edit's right answers are nearly as long as RL plain's (ratio 0.86-1.00), far above the cued base's ratio (0.73), whose opening comes from the cue without RL's derivation change.
consequences.why_new: No fact or listed result compares the edit's right-answer length with RL's on hard328. result-1b6bf2 compares the edit's lengths with the base's only, and F25 is about step 100 on MATH-500.
consequences.statistic: geometric mean over problems of (median right-answer n_new of the edit / median right-answer n_new of RL plain), a ratio with no unit
consequences.rows: attempt 0, samples 0-3 of each cell, score_v3 = 1 only; problems where both cells have at least one right sample
consequences.computation: 1) For each pid and cell, take attempt-0 rows (samples 0-3) with score_v3 == 1, and take the median of their n_new (mean of the two middle values when the count is even). 2) Keep pids where both cells have a median. 3) Statistic = exp(mean over kept pids of ln(median_edit / median_RL)). 4) 90 % interval: 2000 bootstrap resamples of all pids of the half, with replacement; recompute steps 2-3 on each resample; take the 5th and 95th percentiles.
consequences.null: The base's own rows: the same ratio for the cued base (rlneurons/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01, attempt 0) against RL is 0.725 [0.683, 0.777] on explore (n 105). The accuracy-proportional alternative (log length moves with the share of the base-to-RL accuracy gap closed, 1.01) predicts 1.004. Both lie outside the explore interval.

consequences.claim: Sentences 1-2 and 5 say RL's 8 paired directions carry RL's derivation style, and an edit of the same norm in random directions does not. So on code problems that both pass, the Code-RL top-8 1.5x edit's passing answers are about as long as RL-Code's (ratio 0.855-1.035), while the random rank-8 1.5x edit stays at base length (0.67).
consequences.why_new: result-a1bf75 and F36/F37 report pass counts and pass rates of the code dial; no fact or result compares the edit's passing-answer length with RL-Code's on the same problems.
consequences.statistic: geometric mean over problems of (n_new of the Code top-8 1.5x passing answer / median n_new of RL-Code's passing answers over 3 seeds), a ratio with no unit
consequences.rows: every row (one per problem per cell) with passed true; problems where the edit passes and at least one of the 3 RL-Code seeds passes
consequences.computation: 1) For each pid, edit length = n_new of the code_top8x1.5_code31 row if passed. RL length = median n_new over the passed rows of the three rl_plain cells (seeds 51/52/53 M; mean of the two middle values when even). 2) Keep pids with both. 3) Statistic = exp(mean of ln(edit / RL)). 4) 90 % interval: 2000 bootstrap resamples of all pids of the half with replacement, recompute steps 2-3, 5th and 95th percentiles.
consequences.null: A random edit of the same norm: rlneurons/xreward/code_depth/code_rand8x1.5_code31 in place of the edit gives 0.675 [0.624, 0.732] (n 160); the cued base gives 0.653. The accuracy-proportional alternative (share 1.22) predicts 1.099. All lie outside the explore interval.

consequences.claim: Sentences 2-3 say the cue gives the base RL's opening but not RL's longer, checked derivation, while the 1.5x edit gives both. So on MATH-500 problems that both solve, the edit's right answers are close to RL's length (0.81-0.955), far above the cued base's 0.62.
consequences.why_new: result-d82083 and result-95a4dc give only the 1.5x edit's MATH-500 score; F25 compares step 100 with the cued base. No fact or result gives the edit's right-answer length against RL's.

cell.readout: right of 328 (grader v3) for RL plain on hard328 at T 0.6 / top-p 1.0, one sample per problem, seeds 3000000 + index
cell.command: python -m studies.rlneurons.jobs.run_cell --model rl --prompt plain --set hard328 --temperature 0.6 --top-p 1.0 --seed 3000000 --commit COMMIT_SHA
cell.why: Sentences 2 and 4: RL's change cuts the long tail (answers stop instead of looping), so unlike the cued base, RL loses almost nothing when the temperature drops to 0.6. Its hard328 score stays at its T 1.0 level (206, 1-sample binomial spread about +-14), with cap hits near its T 1.0 rate.
